moat_against: Powerful concentrated buyers dual-source with Crown and Ardagh
Can-making is proven, replicable technology — no proprietary lock-in
Pricing is largely cost pass-through; real pricing power is thin
ROIC ~8-10% through the cycle, not well above cost of capital
High leverage: net debt 7.0x normalized OE
moat_for: Largest global beverage-can footprint; plant proximity to customer filling lines is hard to replicate
Long-term supply contracts with major beverage companies
Aluminum recyclability tailwind as brands shift off plastic
Metal cost pass-through in contracts limits commodity margin risk
moat_justification: Scale leadership in a can-making oligopoly with long-term contracts and metal pass-through, but buyers are powerful and dual-sourced, pricing is largely pass-through, and ROIC ran only ~8-10% (roic_proxy 2020-2023 in fundamentals.json) — at, not well above, the cost of capital.
name: Ball Corporation
one_liner: Decent oligopoly can maker, moat 5/10, but levered, cyclical owner's earnings — at $63.20 the weighted IRR is 8.8% (IV@15% $30.86); it only clears 15% below ~$31.
